_rules: Edit only 'passes' (and 'notes'). Set passes=true only after `./init.sh check <id>` exits 0. Items run in order unless deps allow otherwise. Adding new items is fine; deleting or weakening a check is not.
_strategy: Follow Burnout3/xboxrecomp pattern: (1) static checks (compile, fidelity, reachability), (2) smoke tests (boot, menu, no crash), (3) user playtest (manual, crash logs seed static fixes). No replays, no frame limits, no screenshots in checks.

items.desc: Toolchain installed: JDK21, Ghidra headless, emscripten, SDL2, capstone, python venv with capstone+pefile
CLAUDE.md, features.json, PROGRESS.md, init.sh, scripts/run.sh exist; krn state objective set
items.check: test -f CLAUDE.md -a -f PROGRESS.md -a -x init.sh -a -x scripts/run.sh && krn state show | grep -qi rugby

items.desc: pcrecomp pe_analyze + extract_imports → analysis/pe_analysis.json, analysis/imports.json; import count recorded in REVERSE.md
pcrecomp disasm32 → analysis/functions.json with >=15000 functions
Ghidra headless analysis (RTTI on) + pcrecomp ghidra scripts export function bounds CSV to analysis/ghidra_funcs.csv
score_recovery: pcrecomp catalog vs Ghidra; recall >= 0.97 recorded in REVERSE.md; missing starts merged into functions.json
pcrecomp cpp/rtti.py → analysis/vtables.json; class count >= 600 (matches rugby08_classes_and_sources.txt)
python -m tools (pcrecomp translator) lifts every function into gen/; 0 instructions lifted as comments/unsupported
pcrecomp difftest (or our port of it to macOS: run lifted C vs unicorn/x86 emulation) passes on >=500 sampled leaf functions
Lift fidelity: ref_bytes_lifted >= 99%, off_boundary_insns < 2000, ghidra_unlifted <= 20 (encrypted stubs in protector region)
items.check: source .venv/bin/activate && python3 tools/fidelity_report.py 2>&1 | grep -qE 'ref_bytes_lifted=99|off_boundary_insns=([0-9]|[0-9]{2}|[0-9]{3}|1[0-9]{3})[^0-9]' && python3 tools/fidelity_report.py 2>&1 | grep -qE 'ghidra_unlifted=([0-9]|1[0-9]|20)([^0-9]|$)'
items.notes: 2026-10-10: check regex fixed to match its description (ghidra_unlifted <= 20); the old (0|1|2?[0-9]) accepted only 0-9 and 20-29.

items.desc: Strict reachability after ret/jmp: all switch-table arms and EH landing pads are entries; fallthrough_targets_not_lifted < 10
items.notes: Current: 305 not lifted. Root cause: pcrecomp treats every byte after jmp as a potential entry, lifting junk; build_catalog must compute labels from switch/EH tables only. See PROGRESS.md 2026-10-04.

Reference run: the original Rugby08_unpacked.exe runs under Wine (wine-stable, WoW64) for 60 s with d3d8 loaded and no unhandled exception. Tells a bad unpack apart from lifter bugs. Dispatch misses run in a Unicorn interpreter on the same guest memory (runtime/core/interp.c) instead of eax=0; exits back to lifted code on entry/RECOMP_RETADDR. difftest --interp: >=500 lifted functions (leaf and non-leaf) give identical state when interpreted. Plan P2.
Native binary exits cleanly (status 0) after 600 frames: no crash, segfault, or abort; checks CRT init, boot, menu render
items.notes: Ready for user playtest via scripts/play.sh. Crashes logged to logs/native_run.log; seed new issues via tools/icall_seed.py from logs/icall_miss.txt, then re-run tools/lift_fixpoint.sh.

items.desc: Same sources build with emcc (SDL2 port, WebGL2, pthreads) into build/web/
ALL Game Files packaged into chunked lazy-loaded bundles in build/web/data/ (no picker, no fallback); manifest lists every original file
tools/serve.py serves build/web on localhost with COOP/COEP headers

tools/patch_exe.py --full writes a deprotected PE (obfuscated calls, pointer stubs, decrypt-stub switch slots, 0x1055000 dispatcher resolved to direct branches) that runs under Wine like the original; the lift then uses it. Plan P3.
Interpreter fallback in the web build (Unicorn via emscripten) or, if that is not viable, the web lift includes all logs/interp_entries.txt entries and misses stop cleanly. Plan P4.
Browser loads localhost, WASM initializes, WinMain entered (no crash on load)

items.desc: The game's own CRT math (atan2 0x873250, exp 0x874C90 -- both through the fxam-classifying transcendental dispatcher) matches host libm within 1e-12 over a sign/zero/quadrant grid, evaluated at WinMain (RT_SELFTEST_CRT, runtime/core/log.c). Guards the 8-bit sar lift (atan2 returned x for y=0, the run direction was wrong).
items.check: RT_SELFTEST_CRT=1 SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy timeout 120 build/native/rugby08 --frames 10 --log logs/selftest_crt.log 2>&1 | grep -q "crt selftest: .* 0 wrong -> PASS"

items.desc: Deterministic mode: two native runs of play_now_match.txt (RT_DET=1) are state-hash identical at every 300th frame up to frame 15000 (into a match).
Deterministic mode ignores host timing: random host delays at every guest thread hand-over (RT_DET_CHAOS) leave the state hashes unchanged.
Netplay 1v1 over the relay server (server/): two native instances, each driving its own virtual pad, Scotland v New Zealand from Team Select into the match; equal state hashes over 15000 frames.
A desync is detected: one flipped guest byte on one instance (RT_NET_FAULT) stops both with a DESYNC report.
items.check: ! FAULT=500 tools/net_test.sh --frames 1500 --timeout 400 && grep -q DESYNC logs/net_out1.log && grep -q DESYNC logs/net_out2.log

items.desc: Netplay in the browser: two headless Chromium pages join one room through the relay (?net=auto) and keep equal state hashes.
Per-player camera (d3d8_pov.cpp): a camera preset re-projects the match view (screenshot differs from the game camera).
Independent cameras online: player 2 watches through its own camera preset (RT_POV=3) while player 1 uses the game camera; the match state hashes stay equal over 15000 frames.

Live input in real browser pages: the host's (controller 1's) real mouse clicks and keys are the game's own keyboard and mouse and reach the game on both pages at the same frame (original controls, Esc pause); a friend's keyboard is its controller; state hashes stay equal.
items.check: timeout 600 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 tools/net_live_input.py   # system Python: Playwright is not in .venv

items.desc: Drop-in online play (native): player 2 joins 15 s into player 1s running game (player 1 paced at 60 fps), replays the room log, catches up without drawing and plays on with equal state hashes.
The room outlives its creator: player 1 leaves, player 2 takes over admitting newcomers, a third player joins later and agrees with player 2 on every state hash.

Drop-in in real browser pages, as players use it: the game boots straight in, the host's code comes from its Online panel, a friend opens their own game and types the code into the Join box 20 s later, catches up, gets the "You're in" toast, its keys reach its controller, hashes stay equal, and the host plays on after the friend leaves.

The web build's split giant functions behave like the originals: a native build with build/web-gen opens MY RUGBY and Squad Management without a fault (the split jump tables sent computed jumps to the wrong exit; MY RUGBY crashed in the browser).

The CRT math self-test passes in the browser build too, where no interpreter stands behind the lift: every arm of the CRT's x87 dispatcher that the grid reaches (zero, negative, overflow, underflow, infinities, NaN, denormal) is lifted and keeps the calling convention (an unlifted exp arm unbalanced the stack and crashed the game at the first scrum).
Match state found in guest memory and read by runtime/core/match_state.c (docs/MATCH_STATE.md): 30 players, ball, score, clock, phase, controlled player per pad, match setup.
The host's match setup applied on a friend whose own game took another menu route: both reach kickoff with identical setup bytes, same teams and stadium.
Friend mode: local match simulation suppressed, host state applied every frame; a recorded host match plays back in another game within 1 cm for 3000 frames.
Host-authoritative over the server: friends' pads drive their players on the host, host state reaches friends within 6 frames.
Party flow: host starts, friends' own games enter Team Select and the match; pauser drives the pause menu; full time returns everyone to their own menus; twice in one party.
Online screens drawn inside the game (Host code, Join by typing the code, party badge, leave), keyboard/mouse/pad; no HTML panel; native and browser.
Mac native and browser players share one match (both directions).
Server runs with TLS on the user's own server; players' guide in docs/ONLINE.md (deploying needs the user's go).
